window: Tuesday, 6:00 pm to 11:00 pm, after the IFT222 lessons
goal: Module One of the course text: theory Question 1, and the first of your two written answers. The analyst, the life cycle and the methodologies, then the practical on choosing and justifying a methodology. It goes tonight so Friday is not left with the whole course.
drill: In each lesson, do every test question, then the first twenty of Drill every fact (matching first; they cover the most facts). The methodology selection table is the most examined thing here: say it from memory before you sleep. Finish on Learn by Doing: Module One, which is this module sat as a paper: fifty objective questions, then three theory questions with their practicals, each answered twice.

window: Wednesday, 6:30 pm to 11:00 pm, after the IFT222 paper
goal: Module Two of the course text: theory Question 2, your second written answer, and the heaviest diagram work: fact-finding, use cases, data flow diagrams and entity relationship diagrams. Draw each diagram by hand as you meet it, then the practical; this is a drawing paper.
drill: Every test question first, then the first twenty of each Drill every fact. Twenty-one of test 2's thirty questions sit here, and ten of them are matching: learn definitions BESIDE their names. Finish on Learn by Doing: Module Two, the module sat as a paper, and draw every diagram in it by hand.

window: Friday, 12:30 pm to 2:30 pm, after the Java paper
goal: Module Three, for the objective questions: you will write Questions 1 and 2, but Module Three's definitions are among the thirty objective questions. Objects, class diagrams and the behavioural diagrams, then the cram sheet, which also brings back the lists from Modules One and Two. Eat something first.
drill: Include against extend, aggregation against composition, sequence against collaboration: three pairs, all asked. In the hall, answer Questions 1 and 2, and turn to Question 3 only if one of them is far worse than you hoped. Learn by Doing: Module Three is fifty objective questions on this module, and those are the marks Module Three is worth to you. Do Part A even if Part B has to wait.

window: Only if you finish early: past papers and extra practice, not required
goal: The Module Three practical, both past papers and three practice papers, all in the older shape. Practise the questions on Modules One and Two first, since those are the two you will write, and draw every diagram by hand.
drill: If you have any spare minutes at all, sketch Question One of the 2025/2026 paper: it is a Module Two scenario.
